title: useMutate
subtitle: React hook for handling mutations with automatic state management
description: A powerful hook for handling asynchronous mutations (create, update, delete operations) with built-in loading, error, and success states. Features automatic type inference, query invalidation, and lifecycle callbacks.

rows.name: mutationFn
rows.description: The async function that performs the mutation. Types are automatically inferred from this function.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Optional configuration object for callbacks and query invalidation.

rows.name: options.onSuccess
rows.description: Callback fired when the mutation succeeds. Receives the returned data and the arguments passed to mutate.

rows.name: options.onError
rows.description: Callback fired when the mutation fails. Receives the error and the arguments passed to mutate.

rows.name: options.onSettled
rows.description: Callback fired when the mutation completes (success or error). Receives data (or undefined), error (or undefined), and args.

rows.name: options.queryKey
rows.description: Query key to invalidate after mutation completes. Useful for refetching related data.

returns.description: Object containing mutation state and trigger functions

properties.name: mutate
properties.description: Function to trigger the mutation. Errors are caught and stored in state.

properties.name: mutateAsync
properties.description: Function to trigger the mutation and return a promise. Throws on error.

properties.name: isPending
properties.description: True while the mutation is in progress.

properties.name: data
properties.description: The data returned from the last successful mutation.

properties.name: error
properties.description: The error from the last failed mutation, undefined otherwise.

properties.name: reset
properties.description: Resets the mutation state (isPending, data, error) to initial values.

behavior.title: Automatic Type Inference
behavior.description: Data and argument types are automatically inferred from the mutation function

behavior.title: Query Invalidation
behavior.description: Optionally invalidate and refetch queries after mutation completes

behavior.title: Lifecycle Callbacks
behavior.description: onSuccess, onError, and onSettled callbacks for handling mutation results

behavior.title: State Management
behavior.description: Built-in isPending, data, and error state with reset functionality

dos: Use mutate() for fire-and-forget mutations, mutateAsync() when you need the result
Invalidate related queries using the queryKey option to keep data in sync
Handle errors in callbacks or by checking the error state
Use reset() to clear state before showing a form again
Leverage TypeScript - types are automatically inferred from mutationFn
donts: Don't forget to handle loading states in your UI
Don't use useMutate for data fetching (use useQuery instead)
Don't ignore errors - always provide user feedback
Don't create new mutation functions on every render (define outside component or use useCallback)

callouts.title: Type Inference
callouts.content: useMutate automatically infers Data and Args types from your mutation function. No need to specify generics in most cases!

callouts.title: Query Invalidation
callouts.content: Use the queryKey option to automatically refetch related queries after mutation. This keeps your UI in sync without manual refetching.
